posts.title: Building a character-led Instagram account for Midoin
captions: minseo.chung Midoin runs 32+ restaurants, and its official Instagram (about 11K followers) mostly shared menus and promotions. That left room for a second account built on character and storytelling.

Our audience: women in their 20s and 30s (core 22–29) who find restaurants on Reels and Explore, skip anything that looks like an ad, and save and send what feels like their own story. So we created Midori, a picky eater who speaks for them: "a meal worth recording, for picky tastes."
posts.role: Team leader of three. Ran the eight-week timeline and assigned roles, produced Reels and four-panel comics (ChatGPT, Kling AI, CapCut, Canva), and designed the Meta Ads A/B test.

posts.title: From interactive Reels to profile visits
captions: Join: a "solo-dining level test" asked people to comment their level. It led the account in views and follows, and about 90 people joined the event.
Send: a couple's "who pays tonight" roulette drew 73 of the account's 246 shares. Visit: a Reel shot in store drove 41 of 126 profile visits. Paid: a relatable couple scene became the ad creative.

posts.title: Testing one variable: the first frame
captions: minseo.chung Same Reel, same budget, same time. Only the thumbnail changed. The food close-up won on every metric, so we kept it.

insights.title: Ad insights
insights.fine: I designed the test; a teammate operated the ad account.

insights.title: Campaigns against a KPI
insights.intro: Target: 2% link clicks relative to reach. We ran two campaigns with different objectives.
insights.outro: What I took away: match the campaign objective to the KPI you care about.
insights.fine: Allocated paid budget KRW 600,000; KRW 472,907 spent across the two campaigns. Bars scaled to 4%.

posts.location: Korea Foundation Digital Public Diplomacy Academy · Jul–Sep 2026
posts.title: Making Korean café culture easier to explore
captions: minseo.chung Foreign visitors often freeze at Korean café kiosks. Our team of seven built two answers: Who Ordered This?, an iOS game where you make Korean drinks and help customers at a kiosk, and @more_kaffeine, an Instagram magazine on café culture.
posts.role: Ran Meta ads for the magazine's posts, managed the team's KRW 4.5M budget, and built parts of the app backend.

posts.title: "My favorite Korean drink is…"
captions: minseo.chung An Add Yours sticker asked followers for their favorite Korean drink. We reshared each entry with what that drink means in Korea, in English, and kept them in an archive that grew with every entry.

posts.title: An English guide for students arriving from six countries
captions: minseo.chung A four-day international career program for high school students from Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Thailand and more. They read the guide in their second language, on their phones, in an unfamiliar city, so it kept sections short, put the rules first, and gave each venue a bit of local history. Participant guide pages I managed in Notion. Card design by others.
posts.role: Worked on the program from planning to on-site operations. Built the English participant guide in Notion, translated about ten showcase team and game descriptions between Korean and English, and co-planned cultural missions at Jongmyo and Ikseon-dong. I also translated the 20-page 2027 COYC guidelines from JA Asia Pacific into Korean.
posts.fine: Excerpt from the participant-facing guide. Contact numbers and internal details left out.

posts.title: Introducing Korea in French, at a dinner table
captions: K-beauty in class. I gave a K-beauty presentation in French with live product demos, a quiz and giveaways. Several classmates later bought the products. I also visited K-EXPO France 2024.

International Dinner. I invited friends from different countries, chose mild dishes like japchae and bulgogi for those new to spicy food, and asked everyone to bring a dish from home. Before long, friends were asking "What time tonight?" before I had even sent the invite.
